quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What shape is a stop sign?
questions.explanation: Stop signs have eight sides. Only stop signs use this shape. It tells drivers to stop completely.

questions.question: What is most important about speed when driving around curves?

options.text: Drive at the posted speed limit as you enter the curve, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Accelerate gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the posted speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve. Your vehicle may slide on curves. Slowing down helps you stay in control.

questions.question: When turning left, which traffic signal gives you the right-of-way?
questions.explanation: A green arrow lets you turn in that direction. Oncoming traffic stops. You have the right-of-way.

questions.question: What does a red circle with a slash through it mean on a regulatory sign?
questions.explanation: A red circle with a slash means the action is not allowed. These signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and red and black symbols.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. Always follow all posted regulatory signs.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot park in that area. Always follow regulatory signs.

questions.question: What do round signs warn you about?
questions.explanation: Round signs warn of railroad crossings ahead. Be extra careful when you see this sign.

questions.question: What color lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions?
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: How should you enter a freeway?

options.text: Signal, yield to traffic, and enter at the same speed as traffic.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield to you.
Always come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to traffic, and enter at the same speed as traffic.
questions.explanation: Use your signal before merging. Match the speed of other traffic and merge smoothly. Yield to all vehicles already on the freeway.

questions.question: What is the speed limit on blind curves unless otherwise posted?
questions.explanation: The speed limit on blind curves is 20 mph unless a sign shows a different limit. Follow all posted speed limit signs.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen because drivers don't pay attention or act carelessly. Stay alert and watch for other vehicles.

questions.question: Which statement about emergency vehicles is true?

options.text: They have the right-of-way when using sirens and flashing lights.
They may use loudspeakers to give instructions.

questions.explanation: Always yield to police cars, fire trucks, and ambulances when they use sirens and lights. Follow their loudspeaker directions. Emergency vehicles often travel together, so wait until the way is clear before moving.

questions.question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?

options.text: It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system keeps dangerous fumes out of your car. A leak lets carbon monoxide enter the cabin. Fix exhaust leaks right away.

questions.question: You are driving on a two-lane road with no bike lanes. A bicycle is ahead of you, going the same direction. What is the safest way to pass?

options.text: Slow down and wait for no oncoming traffic. Then pass while leaving plenty of space between you and the bicycle.
Keep driving straight. It is the cyclist's job to move out of your way.
Do not pass until you reach a traffic signal or stop sign.
Honk to let the cyclist know you are about to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and wait for no oncoming traffic. Then pass while leaving plenty of space between you and the bicycle.
questions.explanation: Pass a bicycle like you would any other vehicle. Leave at least 3 feet of space. On faster roads, leave at least 5 feet. Do not honk because it can scare the cyclist.

questions.question: Drivers must yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.
If the pedestrian uses a hand signal to ask drivers to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians in the street, even if they cross carelessly or against the light.

questions.question: When driving on wet pavement, remember:

options.text: The road is especially slippery right after it starts to rain.
Leave extra space when you need to stop.

questions.explanation: Wet roads are most slippery right after rain starts. Your tires can lose grip and hydroplane. Slow down and leave extra distance to stop safely.

questions.question: When it starts to sleet or snow, you should:

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.
Leave more distance between your car and the cars ahead.
Be careful around all other vehicles.

questions.explanation: In snow or sleet, keep your windshield and mirrors clear. Increase your distance from other cars because slippery roads make stopping harder.

questions.question: If you stop along the road at night, you should:

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beams on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beams on.
questions.explanation: When stopped on the road at night, turn on your emergency flashers and low beams. This makes your vehicle visible to other drivers.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:

options.text: Can be safely held by a strong adult.
Will be safe if they stand on the floor in the back.
Will not get hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must never be allowed to stand in the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must never be allowed to stand in the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Children need a proper car seat. No adult is strong enough to hold a child safely during a crash or sudden stop. Always use a car seat.

questions.question: At an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk markings, a driver:

options.text: Should slow down to check that crossing traffic is clear.
Should stop far into the intersection where they can see 200 feet in each direction.
Should stop where they can see approaching traffic before entering the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should stop where they can see approaching traffic before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: Stop at the nearest point where you can see traffic coming from all directions. Do not drive into the intersection to get a better view.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road is slippery when wet.
A bump in the road is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and shaped like diamonds. They tell you about hazards ahead. This sign warns you that wet pavement is slippery and harder to control.

questions.question: Which drugs can affect your driving?
questions.explanation: Many drugs affect your ability to drive safely. This includes illegal drugs and legal over-the-counter or prescription medicines. Driving while impaired by any drug is against the law.

questions.question: When you see a solid red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through if no other cars are crossing.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is watching.

questions.explanation: A solid red light means you must stop completely. Driving through a red light is illegal and dangerous. You can turn right on red only if a sign does not forbid it.

questions.question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Release the gas pedal to slow down before braking.

questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for drivers behind you to avoid hitting you. When stopping, release the gas first to slow your car. Then brake smoothly to stop and turn on your brake lights.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the middle of the road mean?

options.text: No passing is allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing is allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass in either direction. The only times you can cross these lines are to turn left or to pass pedestrians, cyclists, or scooter riders when the other lane is clear and safe.
